extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders (inventors, applicants, practitioners, and interested parties) submitting comments to the USPTO on patent or trademark rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments in response to USPTO-specific requests for comment on patent and trademark regulations, including required submission channels, confidentiality cautions, and elements of effective comment content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments through Regulations.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Find, review, and submit comments online for all proposed Federal regulations at Regulations.gov. Comments must be submitted through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Federal eRulemaking Portal for proposed Federal regulations; this is the primary required submission channel for rulemaking comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative submission methods for specific USPTO patent proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: For specific USPTO patent proceedings, comments can also be submitted through other channels: By electronic mail message over the Internet; By postal mail addressed to: Mail Stop Patent Board, Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative channels apply only for certain USPTO proceedings—check the specific proceeding's instructions to confirm permitted submission methods and the correct postal/email destination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact USPTO if electronic submission not feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: If electronic submission is not feasible due to lack of access to a computer/internet, contact the USPTO for special instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify USPTO in advance to obtain alternate submission instructions or accommodations when you cannot use online filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments are public; avoid including private contact info
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments will be made available for public inspection. Information that the submitter does not desire to be made public, such as address or phone number, should not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume submissions become part of the public record; redact or omit personally sensitive information before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe the comment deadline for each proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed rule has its own comment deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm and meet the specific deadline listed for the rulemaking docket you are addressing; late comments may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific patent statute provisions (35 U.S.C. § 100 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should cite specific patent statute provisions (35 U.S.C. § 100 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and reference the statutory provisions that you believe are implicated by the proposed rule to ground your arguments in law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference the MPEP where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should reference the USPTO's Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite MPEP sections or practice guidance that the proposed rule would affect or that support your position on implementation/practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with prior USPTO interpretations and Federal Circuit case law
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should engage with prior USPTO interpretations and Federal Circuit case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how existing agency interpretations or controlling appellate decisions inform or constrain the proposed regulatory approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide data on inventor/applicant impact (especially small inventors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should provide data on inventor/applicant impact (especially small inventors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative or qualitative evidence showing how the proposed rule would affect different stakeholders, with emphasis on small entities where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address cross-Atlantic harmonization with EPO/JPO/other offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should address cross-Atlantic harmonization with EPO/JPO/other offices where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss international practice and potential harmonization or divergence implications for applicants who file internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest specific regulatory text changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should suggest specific regulatory text changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide proposed wording or redlines to the regulatory text to make your recommendations concrete and actionable for policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address fee/cost impacts on different applicant categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should address fee/cost impacts on different applicant categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how fees or cost-related provisions would affect various types of filers (e.g., individual inventors, small entities, corporations) and, if possible, provide dollar estimates or examples.
